crop_profile.summary: Wheat (Triticum aestivum) is a globally important annual cereal grown on loamy to clay soils with pH 6.0-7.5. Optimal temperatures are 10-25 °C, rainfall 300-900 mm/year, and sunlight 6-10 h/day. It requires medium water and nitrogen, with critical moisture needs during flowering. Major producers include China, India, Russia, the United States, and France. Typical yields are 3 t/ha, reaching up to 7 t/ha under optimal management. Key diseases are Fusarium head blight, powdery mildew, and leaf rust; main pests include aphids, Hessian fly, and wheat midge. Integrated pest management, split nitrogen fertilization, and timely harvest ensure high quality grain.

steps.finding: The wheat crop in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu, faces severe heat stress and critical water deficit, as ambient temperatures (30.5°C) exceed optimal thresholds and satellite indicators (NDVI 0.154, NDWI -0.204) confirm severe canopy loss and high water stress. While soil conditions are favorable regarding pH (6.21) and high nitrogen availability, extreme moisture deficit and elevated temperatures severely constrain crop performance. Immediatate intervention via targeted irrigation and mulching is required to prevent crop failure.
steps.consensus: Immediate moisture management and thermal stress mitigation are mandatory to salvage crop health, leveraging adequate baseline soil nitrogen while addressing acute water deficit and low organic carbon.

NDWI (-0.204) is below the high‑stress cutoff (0.0), confirming acute water deficit. SAVI (0.105) is under the high‑exposure limit (0.20), revealing extensive exposed soil and likely poor ground cover. The satellite‑derived health flag of "Critical" aligns with these metrics. Overall, the crop is experiencing extreme water stress, nutrient/possible disease stress, and high soil exposure, all of which threaten yield potential.
